attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter. He states the explanation himself and is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the named firms, the Meta exclusion, 'effectively all', the >70% figure and the clause about data center companies. 'I believe' asserts his own explanation. It is not one of the graded low-confidence hedges, so treating this as a causal claim is reasonable.

contract.note: The plain reading (lab purchases largely explain the growth) is ordinary and fair. The contract correctly leaves open whether >70% applies to the three firms together or to each one. With the current evidence that choice does not change the outcome.

evidence.note: A Bloomberg press estimate for Microsoft only: OpenAI was about 70% of fiscal-year AI sales, based on an assumed total. It does not show >70% across the three firms, near-total compute sales, or causation.

Alphabet's own disclosure names several drivers of Cloud growth. That weighs against a single dominant cause, but it gives no customer shares or quantified contributions, so it does not refute the claim.
CoreWeave's own announcement confirms its direct deal with Anthropic. Delivery was prospective, so it does not show this deal caused the growth already reported.
Runpod's customer list includes OpenAI, so it is not a clean counterexample to the connection claim. It also shows nothing about revenue dependence.

reviews.rationale: The packet has a single press estimate (Microsoft, about 70%, built on assumptions), one company statement listing several growth drivers, and confirmations of connections. Nothing gives comparable lab revenue shares for Google, Amazon and Microsoft, compute allocation records, or growth contributions. No growing, unconnected data center provider is shown. Evidence available by the cutoff neither supports nor refutes the causal claim.
